referendum_required_for: amendments to Chapters I (General Principles), III (Elections, Referendum) and XIII (Introducing Amendments) of the Constitution

government.note: Semi-presidential republic under the 1996 Constitution. In 2000 the directly elected President nominated the Prime Minister for the Verkhovna Rada's consent and could dismiss the government (presidential-parliamentary model). The 2004 amendments (Law 2222-IV of 8 December 2004), in force from 1 January 2006, moved government formation to the Rada majority; in 2010 the 1996 text was restored on the basis of a Constitutional Court ruling, and on 21 February 2014 the Rada reinstated the 2004 amendments. The constitution bars Rada elections while martial law is in effect; elections have been deferred under the martial law in force during the Russo-Ukrainian War.

holders.note: On 22 February 2014 the Verkhovna Rada adopted a resolution that Yanukovych had withdrawn from his constitutional duties and called an early election.
Acting President as Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada (Article 112).
The presidential election due in 2024 was not held under martial law; Zelenskyy remains in office.

offices.note: Under Article 112 of the 2004 text (in force 2006-2010 and since 2014), the Chairperson of the Verkhovna Rada acts as President on a vacancy.

system.note: 1998 and 2002: 225 seats by national closed-list PR (4% threshold) and 225 single-member districts by plurality. 2006 and 2007: all 450 by closed-list PR, 3% threshold. 2012-2019: parallel again with a 5% threshold. Term four years until 2006, five years since. seats_2000 is the result of the March 1998 election by nominating party (list plus district seats); deputies' faction membership changed substantially by 1 January 2000 (the People's Democratic Party faction grew from 29 to 93 after the election, per the source), so this is not the faction composition on that date.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the 1998 Verkhovna Rada list vote: Communist Party 25.4%, Rukh 9.7%, Socialist-Peasant bloc 8.8%, Greens 5.6%, People's Democratic Party 5.2%, Hromada 4.8%, Progressive Socialists 4.2%, SDPU(o) 4.1%, Agrarian Party 3.7%, Reforms and Order 3.1%, National Front 2.7%, and many small lists. Pro-presidential and oligarch-linked centrist lists (NDP, Hromada, smaller centrist blocs) are grouped as big_tent; Kuchma's 1999 re-election (57.7% in the run-off) shows a larger non-communist centre than the list vote. The split among small parties is an estimate.
